test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Rs. 7205 are invested in a scheme of compound interest (compounding annually). If the rate of interest is 20% per annum, then what is the interest earned (in Rs) in 1 year?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For the **first year**, when interest is compounded **annually**, Compound Interest (CI) is equal to Simple Interest (SI).

Interest = 20% of ₹7205

Interest = 7205 ÷ 5

Interest = ₹1441

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1441.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹7205

Rate of Interest (R) = 20% per annum

Time (T) = 1 year

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

Compound Interest (CI) = Amount − Principal

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72106028297fb2bbad81b381006eab6a602eba6ef86143949ef3279a2d31b46e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount = 7205 × (1 + 20/100)¹

⇒ Amount = 7205 × (1 + 1/5)

⇒ Amount = 7205 × (6/5)

⇒ Amount = 1441 × 6

⇒ Amount = ₹8646

⇒ Interest = Amount − Principal

⇒ Interest = 8646 − 7205

⇒ Interest = ₹1441

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1441.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI vs SI for 1st Year

When interest is compounded **annually**, the simple interest and compound interest for the **first year** are always equal.

Compound Interest Formula

The general formula is CI = P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ − 1], where n is the number of conversion periods.

Effective Rate of Interest

If interest is compounded **half-yearly**, the rate becomes R/2 and the time period becomes 2n. For **quarterly**, the rate is R/4 and time is 4n.
